title: Your Life From $0 to Billionaire at Every Level (What It Costs)
hook: Your suit costs $11,000. You're standing at the edge of a grave, not the front — you paid for the flowers, not the eulogy. Twelve years ago you had $52,000 in debt and one truck. This is how you got here — and what it actually cost.
body: POV: you're a first-time small-business owner who borrows $52,000 to buy one used garbage truck and twenty accounts, and spends twenty-four years rolling up a regional waste-hauling company into a $2.6 billion public empire — a blue-collar 'self-made billionaire' arc modeled on the real shape of Wayne Huizenga's 1962 start (one used truck, one route, a roll-up that became Waste Management, Inc.), not a biography. Real, verified mechanics woven in: real 2025-2026 industry acquisition multiples (up to 9.5-11x EBITDA once you own a landfill — the real biggest valuation lever in the business); the real 2024 US average landfill tipping fee (~$62/ton); the real, current OSHA maximum penalty for a willful safety violation ($165,514 per violation); and the episode's core share-worthy fact — real BLS data showing refuse and recyclable collection is the 5th deadliest job in America, with a higher fatality rate than police work, mostly from workers backed over by their own trucks. A dramatized cautionary POV: the founder, the company, the driver, and every named character are a fictional composite; the industry economics, the OSHA penalty structure, and the BLS fatality data are real and independently documented. Watch the whole series — every life, every level, every way the number costs you. For educational and entertainment purposes.
pinned: Real number: refuse and recyclable collection has a higher occupational fatality rate than police work — 37.4 deaths per 100,000 workers in 2024 (BLS), the 5th deadliest job in America. Which level costs the most: the safety line item you cut, or the moment you can't feel the cost of anything anymore?
poll: Which level breaks you first? LEVEL 04 (owning the landfill, $14M) / LEVEL 05 (the buyout offer, cutting the safety budget) / LEVEL 06 (the accident) / LEVEL 09 (the billion, the alarm that never turns off)
